statement: [src] Limine's `tpm_present()` is true when `tpm_init` found either an EFI TCG2 protocol whose `GetCapability` succeeds with `TPMPresentFlag` set, or (only if that failed) an EFI CC measurement protocol (TDX/SEV-SNP confidential computing). Nothing else counts: not a Linux driver, not a firmware setup variable.

[src] Limine v12.9.4 itself writes `LoaderInfo` and `LoaderDevicePartUUID` (the GPT unique partition GUID of the volume it booted from) but no TPM variable. [src] systemd's UKI stub (v262.1) writes `LoaderTpm2ActivePcrBanks` once per boot when no earlier stage set it, as `0x%08x` of `tpm_get_active_pcr_banks()`, which returns 0 when the TCG2 protocol is missing, `GetCapability` fails, `TPMPresentFlag` is clear, or `GetActivePcrBanks` fails; `0xffffffff` for a TCG2 protocol older than 1.1. [src] The TCG EFI Protocol Specification makes a zero mask the defined reply of a platform without a TPM: `TPMPresentFlag = FALSE`, `ActivePcrBanks = 0`.
quote: "If the platform does not have a TPM then the following values SHALL be returned:" (S372 p. 29)

statement: [obs] This boot: `LoaderTpm2ActivePcrBanks` = `0x00000000`, attributes `06` (boot-service + runtime access, not non-volatile, so it does not survive a reboot and is written again each boot); `LoaderInfo` = `Limine 12.9.4`; `LoaderImageIdentifier` = `EFI\Linux\omarchy_linux.efi`; `systemd 262.1-1` ships `/usr/lib/systemd/boot/efi/linuxx64.efi.stub`, whose bytes contain the variable name. [inf] The UKI Limine chainloaded was built on that stub (mkinitcpio's UKI build); its bytes were not read. [obs] Linux side agrees: `/sys/class/tpm/` is empty although `CONFIG_TCG_TIS=y` and `CONFIG_TCG_CRB=y` are built in, no `TPM2`/`TCPA` ACPI table is exposed, and the kernel log has no `tpm` line. [obs] The AMI firmware keeps TCG setup variables (`AMITCGPPIVAR`, `TPMPERBIOSFLAGS`); what they encode was not read.

[inf] So on this host `--tpm-present 0` is the answer for the current boot: the stub's `tcg2_interface_check` is the same LocateProtocol + `GetCapability` + `TPMPresentFlag` test Limine's TCG2 leg makes (TV1, TV2), and it found no present TPM; Limine's CC leg does not apply to a bare-metal AMI board. The stub runs as an image Limine itself started (`LoadImage`/`StartImage`, chainload.c 505-541) while boot services are still up, so it asked the same firmware session. One gap keeps this an inference: a TPM with the flag set whose `GetActivePcrBanks` fails would also read 0. With 0 (or with no `measured_boot` key and Secure Boot off, as here) measured boot is off and every `panic` consequence returns to the menu: the live gate reads `on_panic: menu` without the flag.
source: TV1-TV3, TV9; S361 chainload.c 505-541; S353 menu.c 1719-1728; S362

statement: [src] `guid(X)` and `uuid(X)` are the same dispatcher: X is parsed as a mixed-endian GUID, looked up, then retried big-endian; a text that is not a GUID returns NULL with no message. The lookup compares a volume's `guid` and its GPT unique partition GUID. A partition's `guid` comes from `fs_get_guid`, which returns false for every filesystem in v12.9.4; only a whole-medium volume carries one, the GPT header's disk GUID. So no filesystem UUID ever matches: a `guid()` URI names a partition by its GPT unique partition GUID, or a whole disk by its GPT disk GUID (corrected at landing on wave seat ScoutVolume's finding 1).
quote: "bool fs_get_guid(struct guid *guid, struct volume *part) { (void)guid; (void)part; return false;" (lines 27-30, abridged across lines)

statement: [inf] On this host `guid(b80445be-18ee-45e6-9a30-14339ea785a7)` and `uuid(b80445be-18ee-45e6-9a30-14339ea785a7)` name the ESP (Linux prints PARTUUID in the canonical mixed-endian text the parser expects); `uuid(86D8-C3F6)` — the "UUID" `lsblk` shows for the vfat ESP — names nothing, so on an `efi` entry's `path:` it is a "Failed to open image" panic (UF5).
host_value: ESP has no partition GUID duplicate on the other disks (`lsblk`, before/host/receipt.txt lines 26-41)

statement: [src] `fslabel(L)` compares filesystem labels case-insensitively (`strcasecmp`). [obs] The ESP's vfat label is empty, so no `fslabel()` URI names it on this host.

[src] `boot()` opens the partition Limine booted from; `boot(N)` opens partition N on the same drive. A GPT partition's number is its entry slot plus 1 (`partition + 1`), and empty slots are skipped without renumbering, so N is a slot number with gaps, not a count of partitions (wave seat ScoutVolume's finding 2). [obs] Limine's own `LoaderDevicePartUUID` names `b80445be-…`, the ESP, which Linux numbers partition 1 of `nvme0n1` (Linux numbers GPT slots the same way). [inf] So `boot()` and `boot(1)` name the same volume here. `hdd(d:p)` needs Limine's firmware drive index, which Linux does not show; no `hdd()` URI is mapped.

[obs] An operator check that needs no root: `systemd-analyze has-tpm2` prints `partial` with `-firmware` and `-driver` and exits 3 on this host (its `+system`, `+subsystem`, `+libraries` lines only say the OS could use a TPM). The tool's meaning of `-firmware` was not opened here (wave seat ScoutTPM traced it to the same `LoaderTpm2ActivePcrBanks` variable, `.ufo/waves/round-90/w1/ScoutTPM.md` check 5); read it as a second view of TV3, not an independent probe.
